body.objective: Make the Science Forge launcher rebuild its cached sfc executable whenever any imported Science Forge source changes, not only when sfc.forge itself is newer.
body.stop_condition: Construct a deterministic fixture that builds/caches sfc, changes an imported module such as tools/science-forge/sfc_work.forge without touching sfc.forge, and invokes s-f again. The launcher must detect the changed import closure and rebuild before dispatch. Cache freshness may use a content-addressed import-closure hash or exact dependency manifest; it must also invalidate on compiler or relevant Forge library changes. Add a negative control showing that an unchanged closure reuses the cached executable, a mutation that watches only the root mtime, and clear diagnostics identifying rebuild versus cache reuse. Preserve current explicit SF_BIN/FORGEBIN overrides and run C/native plus sanitizer gates for the affected launcher rail.
body.forbid: no root-file-mtime-only freshness; no directory-mtime heuristic; no unconditional rebuild on every command; no silently stale cached sfc; no physics-repository special case; no bypass of explicit binary overrides
notes: Discovered while validating the Phase-3 SF9 superseding-intent repair: editing sfc_work.forge left the launcher-provided cached sfc stale because freshness considered only sfc.forge.
Hermetic regressions that build a fresh compiler passed; the defect is specifically the resident launcher cache invalidation path.
